runs.hypothesis: The line that names the product. It has to sound like a person describing their week, not an endorsement, so the delivery note asks for matter-of-fact rather than enthusiastic.

input.prompt: Continue the supplied camera frame as one documentary interview take. SUBJECT: the reference bakery owner, greying dark hair tied back; cream long-sleeve shirt, flour-dusted charcoal apron, brown straps, lavalier unchanged. Preserve the visible face, age, hairline, nose, asymmetry and skin texture of the reference; do not beautify or add new facial marks. Fine lines and uneven skin reflect the existing side light. SET: same wood and tile bakery, bread shelves and window on screen right. LIGHT: unchanged warm morning daylight from screen right, stable exposure and white balance. CAMERA: eye-level medium close-up with the original headroom and lens perspective; locked tripod, no zoom, no pan. ENTRY: seated center-left; travel stationary; shoulders relaxed, head upright, mouth closed, gaze slightly camera-right; props microphone clipped to the same apron strap; hands empty below frame. PERFORMANCE: eyes attend to the same interviewer just camera-right, with tiny refocusing movements and unforced irregular blinking. Quiet breath moves the shoulders; one slight head inclination accompanies the thought, then settles. Hands rest low in her lap, not rigid; no finger-counting or presenting objects. Sleeve folds respond only to body movement; stray hairs remain settled in still air. Understated conversational delivery, not a broad smile or theatrical eyebrow lift. AUDIO: say exactly once in natural British English: "We use Crew now. Everyone puts their availability on their phone." Begin promptly, complete the thought without restarting, then let the lips close naturally for a brief listening pause. Quiet bakery room tone, no music. EXIT: shoulders relaxed, head upright, mouth closed, gaze slightly camera-right; seated center-left; travel stationary; props microphone clipped to the same apron strap; hands empty below frame. Same light, set and camera throughout. No cuts, subtitles, titles, logos or graphic overlays.

runs.hypothesis: Compare a single preparation/contact/release chain with repeated turning and tucking; same model and settings, unseeded baseline.

input.prompt: One uninterrupted documentary close-up of a baker's two flour-dusted hands and one round of bread dough on a worn wooden bench. No face. Camera locked in a tight three-quarter view, warm morning side light from screen right, shallow depth of field. Real hand skin with creases, short nails and light flour in the creases, no jewelry. ONE measured action: palms settle on the near half of the dough, lean weight gently forward, compressing it against the bench; fingers remain curved together as the palms release; the elastic dough partly rebounds and stays on the bench. Finish with hands resting lightly alongside the dough for a brief beat. Bench stays fixed, flour smears where skin contacts it; no magical flour cloud. Wrists and forearms carry the force, no floating contact. No second kneading cycle, twisting, fast motion, extra hands, changing dough count, text or logos.
